title: Your First Mini-Program

concept.heading: Combining everything you know
concept.body: You have learned print(), variables, sequential execution, and comments. Now you will combine all four to write your first complete mini-program — a simple student introduction card. Real programs are just many small pieces like these, stacked together in the right order.

analogy.heading: Think of it this way
analogy.body: You now know four basic LEGO bricks. By themselves, each brick is simple. But when you connect them in a sequence, you can build something real. Your first mini-program is like your first small LEGO creation — it is not fancy, but it is entirely yours, and it works.

code_example.code:
# Student Introduction Card
# Module 1 - Final Lesson

# Store student information
first_name = "Eden"
last_name = "Lincuna"
course = "BSIT"
year_level = 3

# Display the introduction
print("=== Student Introduction ===")
print("Name:", first_name, last_name)
print("Course:", course)
print("Year Level:", year_level)
print("===========================")

annotations.note: File-level comment describing what this program does.
We store all the data first — this is a good habit. Define your variables before you use them.
year_level is a number (no quotes). We will use it differently than text variables in future modules.
Printing a separator line using === makes the output look clean and organized.
We pass three things to print(): the label text, and two variables. Python spaces them automatically.
Closing separator — matches the opening line to frame the output like a card.

expected_output:
=== Student Introduction ===
Name: Eden Lincuna
Course: BSIT
Year Level: 3
===========================
key_rule: Store your data in variables first, then display it. This pattern — store then show — is the foundation of almost every program you will ever write.

try_it_yourself.prompt: Build your own Student Introduction Card using your real information. It must include at least: your name, your course, and one other detail of your choice (favorite subject, hometown, or year level).
try_it_yourself.starter_code:
# Student Introduction Card

# Store your information here


# Display your introduction here
try_it_yourself.hint: Follow the same pattern: define your variables at the top, then use print() to display them below. Add comments to explain each section.
